title: Microbial community structure of Penaeus vannamei post-larvae naturally infected with multiple viruses in hatchery tanks
content:
by Betsy Andrade, Mery Ramírez, Guillermo Reyes

Background

This study offers an observational evaluation of how viral and bacterial infections co-occur with alterations in the microbiome and survival of Penaeus vannamei post-larvae, one of the most economically important species in global aquaculture.

Methods

Eleven commercial larval production tanks were classified into three distinct infection scenarios using histology and PCR: Baculovirus penaei (BP) monoinfection, mixed infections (BP, white spot syndrome virus [WSSV], and acute hepatopancreatic necrosis disease [AHPND]-causing bacteria), and non-infected controls. High-molecular-weight DNA was subjected to shotgun metagenomic sequencing on the Illumina NovaSeq 6000 platform, followed by evaluation of microbial diversity, community structure, and infection-associated microbial signatures.

Results

Although BP was the most abundant viral genus across infected groups, severe mortality was observed only under mixed-infection conditions, which were closely associated with AHPND-causing bacteria presence and microbiome disruption rather than with BP alone. Deep metagenomic sequencing revealed reduced, distinct microbiome structures in shrimp infected with BP and in those with mixed infections, compared to non-infected individuals. Non-infected post-larvae maintained complex and well-balanced bacterial communities, predominantly composed of Donghicola and Muricauda. Nudiviridae and Oscillospiraceae showed comparable relative abundances in BP-only and mixed-infection groups. In contrast, mixed infections were characterized by a relative increase in Vibrio, together with the PCR-detection of PirAB toxin genes, whereas WSSV remained detectable in the metagenomic dataset despite its comparatively low relative abundance, while the infection remained thermally suppressed and asymptomatic in the larvae. Functionally, infected larval microbiomes were enriched for transposases, retrotransposons, and virulence-factor genes. The near-complete BP-GR25 genome (119,245 bp) was assembled and annotated from larval metagenomes.

Conclusion

These results highlight the value of high-throughput sequencing in the early detection of pathogens in aquaculture, where subtle microbial shifts during postlarval stages can be valuable indicators of health status for production.
